claims.text: Refractory alloying elements have a significant positive heat of mixing with Cu.
Machine-learning-based interatomic potentials can accurately predict thermodynamic properties of RHEAs.
Machine-learning-based interatomic potentials can accurately predict phase behavior of RHEAs.
The demonstrated predictive capability of machine-learning potentials transfers from TaVCrW to RHEA-Cu composites.
Machine-learning-potential simulations can facilitate development of a method for large-scale reaction in RHEA-Cu composites.
Machine-learning-potential simulations can facilitate development of a stable RHEA-Cu composite microstructure.
Microstructure and phase behavior act as structural mediators for the stability of RHEA-Cu composites.
The proposed computational intervention will improve the high-temperature stability of RHEA-Cu composite structures.
The proposed computational intervention will improve the microstructure of RHEA-Cu composite structures.
Current methods for forming RHEA-Cu composite structures are hindered by positive heat of mixing.
DFT-based ab initio molecular-dynamics calculations of thermodynamic properties are computationally expensive.
The computational cost of conventional DFT-based thermodynamic integration impedes high-throughput calculations.
Current molecular-dynamics methods are limited in their ability to predict RHEA thermodynamic properties and phase behavior.
RHEAs are relevant to elevated-temperature applications because of their resistance to softening and high melting points.
Nuclear-reactor materials can be exposed to extreme temperature, radiation, and stress.
Oxidation and radiation damage may affect the stability and microstructure of RHEA-Cu composites.
